correctness.rationale: Unnormalized Fourier diagonalization gives lambda_{d,k}=1+(d-2k)q+tail. For dq<=2 the common tail bound R<=q^2(e^2-3)<q shows the unique minimum is parity. Decreasing absolute terms from binomial weight two onward show B_d>0 for d<=floor(1/q). At d=floor(1/q)+2, B_d<0 and all larger dimensions inherit the negative principal submatrix. One polynomial determines the intervening dimension and its rank-one boundary. The derivative bound proves one critical root q_d for each d>=17 and a binomial expansion gives q_d=1/d+1/(2d^3)+O(d^-4). check.py ran 327 exact/rational tests and four 70-digit root brackets. The mathematical proof covers infinitely many dimensions and all continuous parameters in scope.

value.rationale: The intrinsic squared-Hamming Gaussian is a natural distance-based covariance whose positivity, unlike the chordal Gaussian, is not guaranteed. The result gives for every sufficiently strong damping a sharp maximal binary-cube dimension, with a one-integer boundary test, a unique parity obstruction, a rank defect exactly one at equality, and a quantified asymptotic critical correction. These infinite-family structural facts are useful for deciding whether an entire Hamming dataset admits a positive-semidefinite covariance and go beyond running a standard Fourier transform or recomputing a finite table.
